summary: Bind FFI lengths and parity to actual bytes buffers

delivery.outcome: Normalize bytes subclasses from their actual buffer before native backend dispatch; align pure-Python reference and compiled/Rust behavior, preserve ordinary bytes identity, regressions and canonical standard. Publish and independently merge under repeated user continuation/test/merge request.
nonGoals: Change C ABI, Rust algorithm, dependency versions, public API signatures or protected delivery policy.
Publish to registries, add platforms or migrate consumers.
Execute native code with an oversized or otherwise invalid buffer length.

architecture.decision: For bytes subclasses only, read the buffer protocol into exact immutable bytes using memoryview.tobytes before both backends and reference iteration. Exact bytes retain the original object. Stub-only oversized-length regression avoids native invalid reads; installed parity uses safe underreported length and hook variants.
architecture.rollback: Revert through independent protected review; retain the capture-stub reproduction and validation receipts without unsafe native replay.

validation.evidence: Oversized subclass length is tested through a Python-only kernel stub; exact bytes identity is preserved; installed backend/reference parity covers ordinary and misleading len/iteration/bytes-hook subclasses.
Full native package build/install, ABI/integrity and C/Rust/Python consumers pass.
Canonical standard metadata/index/source and local checks pass; required governance checks and independent exact-head approval/merge govern delivery.
